title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 31-33). L is a planar or surface-like object cut up by 'découpages' Φ, families of pseudo-lines or pseudo-tracts T_i. M = Mod(L) is a family of distinguished subsets X = X_Φ that L's cuttings define. The image and the next page ('{X,X'} modérée') suggest that 'Mod' may stand for 'modéré(e)' (tame) rather than 'modulaire'. M carries three structures: (a) inclusion; (b) a symmetric 'compatibility' relation, '{X,Y} mod.', meaning X and Y are jointly tame or definable by a common cutting; (c) a subfamily M_f of 'franche' parts, defined by 'franc' pseudo-tracts, which plays the role of closed sets.

Axioms on p.32:
1) M has a least element ∅ and a greatest element 1 = Σ.
2) Comparable elements are compatible.
3) For a compatible pair, the meet X∧Y and join X∨Y exist. A struck-out version asked for distributivity X∧(∨Y_i) = ∨(X∧Y_i) for 'multiplicatively compatible' families.
4) For each X, the set of Y compatible with X and disjoint from it has a largest element X'. X' is also the unique compatible element with X∧X' = ∅ and X∨X' = 1. Hence X ↦ X' is an order-reversing involution (an orthocomplementation). It preserves compatibility and satisfies De Morgan on compatible pairs.
5) ∅ and 1 are franc.
6) Each X has a least franc element containing it, X̄, a closure operator. On compatible pairs it is additive: closure(X∨Y) = X̄∨Ȳ.
7) Compatibility is preserved under closure in either variable.

Left margin: a compatible family generates a (finite) Boolean sublattice for ∧, ∨ and '. A further margin note warns that X∨Y is not the set-theoretic union X∪Y.

Next page: the boundary is defined as Fr X = X̄ ∧ closure(X'), and interiors X° by duality. Tame boundaries are considered, and 'nowhere-dense' elements are characterized. Then the abstract object is introduced: an ordered set satisfying 1)-7), written in Boolean-ring notation (X+Y = (X∨Y)∧(X∧Y)', XY = X∧Y).

In modern terms, Grothendieck is axiomatizing a partial Boolean algebra / orthomodular-poset-like structure, with a compatibility relation and an orthocomplement, equipped with a Kuratowski-type closure operator. It is a 'partial closure algebra'. The aim is to recover point-set topology (closure, interior, boundary) of tame subsets intrinsically from the combinatorics of cuttings, without assuming that arbitrary unions or intersections are tame.
errors: Not an error but a gap: 3) is only justified by 'cf. ex. supra'. That the join of a compatible pair is not the set union (margin warning) means the claimed lattice laws, e.g. De Morgan in 4), depend on facts about tame parts not proved on this page.
In 4), uniqueness of a complement requires something like orthomodularity or distributivity on compatible families. It is assumed via the margin's Boolean-subalgebra condition rather than derived.
Uncertain: the asterisked claim 'if {X,Y} compatible then {X',Y'} compatible' is partially revised in the margin ('en fait ∀X,Y ...'), so its exact final form is unclear.

ideas.what: Set of tame parts with a symmetric compatibility relation; compatible pairs have meet and join; compatible families generate Boolean subalgebras
ideas.modern_name: Partial Boolean algebra / orthomodular poset (compatibility = commensurability)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kochen–Specker (1965); orthomodular posets: Birkhoff–von Neumann (1936), Foulis, Gudder and others

ideas.what: Order-reversing involution X ↦ X' as largest compatible disjoint element; De Morgan laws on compatible pairs
Distinguished 'franc' elements and a least franc element over X, additive on compatible pairs; boundary Fr X = X̄ ∧ closure(X')
ideas.modern_name: Closure algebra / Kuratowski closure operator on a Boolean algebra

ideas.what: Recovering topology of tame subsets from combinatorics of cuttings by pseudo-lines (tame topology program)
ideas.modern_name: o-minimal / tame topology; combinatorial pseudoline arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (o-minimality, 1984-86); Esquisse d'un programme for the program
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 'topologie modérée', only as a program

ideas.what: Boolean-ring notation X+Y = (X∨Y)∧(X∧Y)', XY = X∧Y for the partial structure

missed.claim: In axiomatizing tame (modérées) subsets, Grothendieck independently arrives at the structure of a partial Boolean algebra / orthomodular poset: a compatibility relation, an orthocomplement, and compatible families generating Boolean subalgebras. These are structures from quantum logic. He then enriches them with a Kuratowski closure operator. A link between tame topology (definable sets that are not closed under arbitrary Boolean operations unless 'compatible') and partial Boolean algebras / quantum-logic structures does not seem to be made in the literature.
missed.quote: Si {X,Y} modulaire, X∧Y et X∨Y existent ... prenons les Y∈M tels que {X,Y} modulaire, et X∧Y=φ, il y a un plus grand élément X'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Suggests treating families of tame sets that are not globally definable (e.g. sets tame relative to different cuttings) via partial Boolean algebras / sheaf-theoretic Boolean contexts, as in topos approaches to quantum theory and contextuality. It also suggests an intrinsic 'partial closure algebra' axiomatization of tame topology.

missed.claim: On p.31 Grothendieck asks whether the compatibility relation is determined by the order alone (e.g. via existence of X∧Y). In orthomodular lattices compatibility is determined by order plus orthocomplement (X = (X∧Y)∨(X∧Y')). His question in the tame-topology setting appears unresolved here.
missed.quote: Cette relation est-elle déterminée par la relation d'ordre — p.ex. {X,Y} mod. ssi X∩Y existe ???
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A concrete question about whether tame-set compatibility is order-theoretically recoverable, analogous to known results on orthomodular posets.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful axiomatization whose individual ingredients (orthocomplementation, closure algebra, Boolean subalgebras generated by compatible families) are known. Notable is that Grothendieck's tame-topology program leads him to a partial-Boolean-algebra-with-closure structure, a connection to quantum-logic structures that is unremarked. Still elementary.
transcription_corrections: 'modulaire' (and 'Mod(L)') may well be 'modéré(e)' (tame); the next page writes '{X,X'} modérée'. The handwriting 'm-odéré' is compatible with this.
Margin diagonal plausibly reads 'Dire une famille {X_i}_{i∈I} ⊂ M multiplicativement modérée si ... sous-réseau booléen ... (stable par ∧, ∨, ' ...) fini ...'; compare 'mult mod' in the struck 3).
Item 6) appears as '6) ∀X∈M, il existe un plus petit Y∈M_f tel que X⊂Y (on pose Y = X̄)', and item 7) is renumbered from 6).
